# @writingmate/auth

Sign in to the Writingmate API from coding agents with your Writingmate account, instead of pasting a long-lived API key.

- Requests are paid from your **plan credits**, the same as chatting in the app.
- Access tokens last under an hour and refresh on their own. You sign in again every 48 hours.
- For servers and unattended jobs, use a [Developer API key](https://writingmate.ai/docs/chat-ai-models/openai-compatible-api) instead; those are paid with extra credits.

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

## OpenCode

Add the plugin to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@writingmate/auth"]
}
```

Sign in, choosing **Writingmate** and then **Sign in with Writingmate (uses your plan)**:

```bash
opencode auth login
```

Then use any Writingmate model:

```bash
opencode run -m writingmate/google/gemini-2.5-flash "say hi"
```

The plugin adds Writingmate as a provider with two starter models. To use others, list them under `provider.writingmate.models` in `opencode.json`; any model id from `GET https://writingmate.ai/api/openai/v1/models` works.

## Other tools

The package also installs a small command for tools that can run a command to get a token:

```bash
npx @writingmate/auth login    # sign in with your browser
npx @writingmate/auth token    # print a fresh access token
npx @writingmate/auth status   # show the current sign-in
npx @writingmate/auth logout   # remove the sign-in from this machine
```

`token` prints only the token, so it can be used as `$(npx @writingmate/auth token)` or as a tool's token command. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to `https://writingmate.ai/api/openai/v1`.

## Where the sign-in is stored

OpenCode keeps it in its own credential store. The command-line tool keeps it in `~/.config/writingmate/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/writingmate/`), readable only by your user. Set `WRITINGMATE_AUTH_FILE` to use another path.
